## 3. Exact construction: integrate the remaining photons before sampling

Define

\[
D=A+VC(I-C^2)^{-1}V^T,\qquad
E=V(I-C^2)^{-1}V^T,
\]

and

\[
K=\begin{pmatrix}D&E\\E&D\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Repeat each herald label \(h_i\) times in each half to obtain the \(2H\times2H\) matrix \(K_h\). Its entries are nonnegative because the inverses expand as convergent nonnegative series.

The herald probability is

\[
\boxed{
P_B(h)
=
\sqrt{\frac{\det(I-B^2)}{\det(I-C^2)}}
\frac{\operatorname{haf}K_h}{\prod_i h_i!}.
}
\tag{1}
\]

Here the hafnian is the positive weighted perfect-matching sum. Exact matching feasibility therefore detects zero herald probability.

### The complete probability-generating function

Let \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(z_1,\ldots,z_r)\), and define

\[
\begin{aligned}
D(Z)
&=
A+\sum_{k\ge0}VZ(CZ)^{2k+1}V^T,\\
E(Z)
&=
\sum_{k\ge0}VZ(CZ)^{2k}V^T,\\
K(Z)&=
\begin{pmatrix}D(Z)&E(Z)\\E(Z)&D(Z)\end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Then the conditional photon generating function is exactly

\[
\boxed{
G_h(Z)
=
\sqrt{\frac{\det(I-C^2)}
{\det(I-(ZC)^2)}}
\frac{\operatorname{haf}K_h(Z)}
{\operatorname{haf}K_h(I)}.
}
\tag{2}
\]

This identity specifies every joint photon probability.

To derive it, introduce the unnormalized generating state

\[
|\Phi(x)\rangle
=
e^{x^TAx/2}
e^{a^\dagger V^Tx+a^{\dagger T}Ca^\dagger/2}|0\rangle.
\]

The conditional state is proportional to
\(\partial_x^h|\Phi(x)\rangle|_{x=0}/\sqrt{h!}\).
Gaussian contraction gives

\[
\langle\Phi(x)|Z^{N_R}|\Phi(y)\rangle
=
\frac{
\exp\!\left[
\frac12x^TD(Z)x+x^TE(Z)y+\frac12y^TD(Z)y
\right]}
{\sqrt{\det(I-(ZC)^2)}}.
\]

Differentiating \(h\) times in both copies pairs the \(2H\) herald derivatives. Those pairings give the hafnian. Normalizing at \(Z=I\) proves (2).

Gaussian integral and hafnian descriptions of heralded states are established machinery. The additional construction here is to turn this expression into a positive, fully sampled process with a herald-dependent matching size and an acquired runtime bound. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

### Sampling the three components

**First, sample one matching on the \(2H\) ports.** Its weight is the product of the corresponding entries of \(K_h(I)\).

**Second, decorate each matching edge by an open walk.**

- An edge within one half uses either its direct \(A_{ij}\) contribution, producing no remaining photons, or a walk with a positive even number of remaining-mode visits.
- An edge between halves uses a walk with an odd number of visits.

These walks can be sampled without rejection on a rare endpoint. Introduce the parity lift

\[
Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&C\\C&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For the required terminal and exit parity, let \(b\) contain the terminal weights, and solve

\[
g=(I-Q)^{-1}b.
\]

At a state \(u\) with \(g_u>0\), use

\[
P(\mathrm{stop}\mid u)=\frac{b_u}{g_u},
\qquad
P(u\to v)=\frac{Q_{uv}g_v}{g_u}.
\tag{3}
\]

These probabilities sum to one because \(g=b+Qg\). The initial vertex has weight \(V_{iu}g_{(u,0)}\). Since \(\rho(Q)<1\), absorption occurs almost surely.

**Third, add independent even closed walks.** For each even length \(\ell\ge2\), the number of loops is Poisson with mean

\[
\lambda_\ell=\frac{\operatorname{tr}C^\ell}{\ell}.
\tag{4}
\]

The identity behind this component is

\[
\log G_{\mathrm{loops}}(Z)
=
\sum_{\substack{\ell\ge2\\\ell\ \mathrm{even}}}
\frac{\operatorname{tr}(ZC)^\ell-\operatorname{tr}C^\ell}{\ell}.
\]

For a chosen length, select root \(j\) with probability proportional to \((C^\ell)_{jj}\). With \(t\) steps remaining, a bridge transition is

\[
P(u\to v)
=
\frac{C_{uv}(C^{t-1})_{vj}}{(C^t)_{uj}}.
\tag{5}
\]

Again, closure is acquired directly. Counting every visit from the open and closed walks gives the sampled photon configuration.
